primary_coaching_focus.quote: And if you if you do want to potentially remove that tree, just give me a callback, and then we can build a design as if that tree was gone.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer never fully disqualified himself ('it depends which tree') but the rep left the entire next step in the customer's hands with no date or follow-up mechanism, likely losing a workable lead to inertia rather than a hard gate.

key_moments.stewart_read: An anomalous opening line before the customer even answers — likely a self-correction or crosstalk artifact, but it means the call starts with zero legitimacy framing captured on tape before the customer picks up.

key_moments.quote: I'm assuming you're gonna say that probably doesn't make this a worthwhile venture.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer hands the rep an opening to reframe — he's testing whether the rep will confirm defeat or create curiosity about a design workaround. The rep's very next line agrees with the pessimistic frame instead of using it as a hook.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. That's what I would probably say.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the moment the rep validates the objection on its own terms rather than inverting it — the schema's guidance is to use the customer's framing as a pattern interrupt, not to co-sign it.

This is a real qualification-preserving signal — the customer is not flatly refusing tree removal, he's negotiating which tree, which means the home may still be workable. The rep's follow-up narrows to one tree but never quantifies impact or urgency around it.
